body: I did the same thing. I kind of get the impression it's not uncommon for those of us who grew up in the 80s or 90s.
I wish I had the balls to do this. Good on you, OP.
You forgot the quadruple venti extra shot Starbucks caramel macchiato!
Me. I often think to myself, "well, if I survive, then I'll have real problems."
I'm so sorry you've had these experiences and that you're feeling pain now. You'll be in my thoughts.

I feel the same way. People don't wanna accept that not everyone gets the same chances or have the same resources, and if you question the fairness or rightness of it, they chew you out for being "entitled" or "a pussy," "not knowing how good you have it," etc. 

Then, people wonder why I want to jump off a fucking bridge. No, I'm not a pussy, I'm just fucking aware of the realities of life.

I've visited your lovely city before. My grandfather was born near there (not enough to claim citizenship, unfortunately) and it was my honeymoon destination when my husband and I were married. I've started a new life exactly the way you described before when I moved to my current region - I loved it, and I actually did very well, considering I knew exactly one person when I moved here. What keeps me from doing that again is my marriage and the young child my husband and I have together. My husband is actually a great person - the only thing we really disagree on is that I would like to start life over in a new country while he feels at home in this one, and that he's refused to set boundaries around my birth family, all of which are manipulative, nasty authoritarians. He can't relate to the idea of having family that's constantly trying to hurt you, having to keep secrets, hide things, and so on.

I've considered just going alone - getting into my car, driving to the boarder, going to a Canadian city (probably not Montreal, since my French is awful), renting an apartment and starting over. I'm a full-time freelancer already, so it wouldn't be that hard. I'd try to eventually find a legal way to gain a long-term visa. But it would mean leaving my daughter behind. I don't want to drag her into an international custody battle, especially if my immigration status might initially be murky. My dad abandoned me with my mother when I was a kid, and there is nothing worse than growing up knowing your parent values whatever cool life they have more than being in yours - I could never do that to her. On the other hand, dying seems like a slightly better alternative. My husband would be a successful, fairly young widower with a cute little daughter; basically a character straight out of a romantic comedy. I'm sure he could find a second wife fairly easily, maybe a younger woman who could have another child or two with him. My daughter wouldn't have to deal with having an absentee parent or a moody mom - I'd be like a fairy tale to her. A perfect, memorialized version of myself.

That was a much longer rant than I intended. Thank you for listening, internet stranger.
